name: Book Evaluation Dataset v1 + v2
description: Books evalset v1 — BOTH request shapes (PR-4 step zero): five cases carry user:preferences (the documented API-contract path) and five carry none (the shape 100% of prod traffic takes since MYS-392, issue #221). Preference-free cases are scored on 5 dimensions (no preference_adherence); gates read the shapes separately via the by_shape summary.

locations.description: Home of the Hobbiton Movie Set, the real-world Shire
Mount Ngauruhoe doubled as Mount Doom; active volcanic landscape
Filming location for the Misty Mountains and Ithilien sequences
Where Tolkien lived, taught, and wrote The Lord of the Rings
must_visit: Eagle and Child pub (Inklings meeting place)

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Must include New Zealand filming locations and UK Tolkien biography sites; should not confuse fictional Middle-earth with real geography
quality_criteria.preference_adherence: Adventure preference must be reflected with specific hiking trails, outdoor activities, and trek difficulty notes at each location
quality_criteria.completeness: Must cover both New Zealand (Hobbiton, Tongariro, Queenstown) and UK (Oxford/Birmingham) with specific landmarks
quality_criteria.actionability: Should include trail difficulty ratings, booking requirements for Hobbiton, and seasonal hiking advice
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: New Zealand and UK locations must be real, accurately named, and correctly attributed to filming
quality_criteria.engagement: Should evoke the epic scope of the journey and connect outdoor experiences to specific scenes from the book

locations.description: Stephen King's home city in Maine; his primary residence and inspiration for many works
must_visit: Stephen King's home on West Broadway

locations.description: Largest city in Maine along the fictional Walk corridor; real King filming and event location
Maine's state capital along the US-1 corridor the fictional Walk follows

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Must surface real Maine/New England locations as the geographic inspiration for the fictional Walk route; should correctly identify King's Bangor connections
quality_criteria.completeness: Should cover Bangor (King biography), the Maine coastal corridor, and at least acknowledge the Walk's fictional endpoint near Boston
quality_criteria.actionability: Should include practical road-trip routing along US-1 and specific King-related addresses
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All locations must be real and in Maine or New England; fictional Gatlin or Walk checkpoints should not be treated as real places
quality_criteria.engagement: Should connect the bleak Maine landscape to the novel's atmosphere of endurance and dread

locations.description: Home base of Ty Franck and Daniel Abraham (the two authors behind James S. A. Corey)
must_visit: University of New Mexico (where Franck worked)
Sandia Mountains (dramatic landscape echoing Martian terrain)

locations.description: Location of the UN headquarters featured in the series as Earth's governing body
must_visit: Intrepid Sea, Air and Space Museum

locations.description: NASA Johnson Space Center — the closest real-world hub to the series' space exploration themes
Maryland city with strong connections to The Expanse's themes of urban decay and resilience

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Must acknowledge the series is space-set and pivot gracefully to author biography and Earth locations from the novels; should not invent space travel destinations
quality_criteria.preference_adherence: Science and space interests should drive the itinerary toward NASA, astronomy, and technology venues
quality_criteria.completeness: Should cover author biography sites and at least two real-world Earth locations with connections to the series' themes
quality_criteria.actionability: Should provide practical visiting info for NASA/space venues and explain their connection to the series
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: No fictional asteroid belt or Mars locations; all destinations must be real Earth locations
quality_criteria.engagement: Should frame the Earth locations through the lens of the series' near-future extrapolation without hallucinating impossible travel

locations.description: Prince Henry's home city; Kensington Palace, St James's Park, and the royal geography central to the novel
must_visit: St James's Park (Henry and Alex's secret meeting spot)

locations.description: Alex Claremont-Diaz's home as First Son; the White House and Georgetown form the novel's American backbone
Setting of the MoMA gala scene and the novel's most publicly romantic moments

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Must include London royal landmarks (Kensington Palace, St James's Park), Washington DC First Family locations (White House area, Georgetown), and NYC MoMA scene; should connect each stop to specific plot moments
quality_criteria.completeness: Should cover London (Henry's world), Washington DC (Alex's world), and at least one shared neutral city such as NYC; hidden gem cafés should feature at each stop
quality_criteria.actionability: Should include specific café and restaurant recommendations, Kensington Palace booking guidance, and a suggested split of days between cities
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All locations must be real and correctly placed; fictional White House interiors should not be treated as visitable spaces — focus on surrounding public areas
quality_criteria.engagement: Should capture the novel's wit, warmth, and the tension of a very public romance — framing each location through the lens of stolen moments and political scrutiny

locations.description: García Márquez's birthplace and the real-world model for the fictional Macondo
Where García Márquez spent much of his later life; the walled city appears in several of his works
Colombia's capital and home to the García Márquez foundation and major literary institutions

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Must identify Aracataca as Macondo's inspiration and connect Cartagena and Bogotá to the author's biography and Colombian historical context
quality_criteria.preference_adherence: Budget options must be highlighted: free museums, street food, budget guesthouses in La Candelaria and Cartagena
quality_criteria.completeness: Should cover Aracataca (literary pilgrimage), Cartagena (author's city), and Bogotá (cultural capital) with specific landmarks
quality_criteria.actionability: Should include practical travel notes between cities (bus vs. flight costs) and free/low-cost museum entry days
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All Colombian locations must be real and accurately located; fictional Macondo should be clearly distinguished from Aracataca
quality_criteria.engagement: Should evoke the humid Caribbean heat and cyclical melancholy of the Buendía family saga

locations.description: Home to the largest Afghan diaspora community in the US, known as Little Kabul; mirrors Amir's California life in the novel
must_visit: Little Kabul district on Fremont Blvd

locations.description: Where Amir and Baba settle after fleeing Afghanistan; Golden Gate Park flea market features in the story
must_visit: Golden Gate Park flea market area

locations.description: Heart of the novel's childhood scenes; travel requires careful planning given current security conditions

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Must include Fremont's Little Kabul community, San Francisco Bay Area Amir connections, and Kabul cultural sites
quality_criteria.completeness: Should cover both the US diaspora locations and Afghan cultural heritage, with the Kabul section framed appropriately given current travel conditions
quality_criteria.actionability: Must include a responsible travel advisory for Afghanistan and practical guidance on experiencing Afghan culture safely in the Bay Area as an alternative
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: Accurate California geography and Afghan locations; Fremont's Little Kabul area must be correctly identified
quality_criteria.engagement: Should honour the emotional weight of the novel's themes of displacement and return without romanticising conflict zones

locations.description: The entire novel unfolds in the streets, canals, and tenements of 19th-century St. Petersburg

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Must include Sennaya Square, the canal district around Griboedov Canal, Dostoevsky Memorial Museum, and Stolyarny Lane; locations must match the novel's geography
quality_criteria.preference_adherence: Solo academic framing should produce an intellectually rich itinerary with reading suggestions, walking routes, and literary context rather than generic sightseeing
quality_criteria.completeness: Must trace Raskolnikov's walking route through the city and include the Dostoevsky Museum as a primary stop
quality_criteria.actionability: Should provide a self-guided walking route with approximate distances and museum opening times
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All St. Petersburg locations must be real and correctly placed in the Haymarket/canal district; no conflation with other Russian cities
quality_criteria.engagement: Should convey the oppressive summer heat, canal smells, and psychological intensity of Raskolnikov's world

locations.description: Strayed's PCT starting point in Southern California; brutal heat and desert landscape
must_visit: PCT Monument at the Mexican Border

locations.description: Gateway to the Sierra Nevada section; pivotal resupply point in the memoir
One of the most dramatic landscapes in Strayed's Oregon section
Strayed's endpoint at the Bridge of the Gods on the Oregon-Washington border

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Must include the Mojave starting stretch, Kennedy Meadows, Oregon sections, and Cascade Locks Bridge of the Gods ending; locations must match Strayed's actual route
quality_criteria.completeness: Should cover Southern California start, Sierra Nevada midpoint, and Oregon finish with resupply town logistics
quality_criteria.actionability: Must include PCT permit information, resupply town options, and recommended gear for each section
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All PCT sections must be real and accurately placed in California and Oregon; no fictional trail segments
quality_criteria.engagement: Should capture the physical and emotional arc of the hike — isolation, endurance, and catharsis

locations.description: Gateway to Transylvania; base for visiting Bran Castle (the popular Dracula castle)
must_visit: Bran Castle (accessibility: partial — lower floors accessible, tower stairs not)
Peles Castle in nearby Sinaia (good accessibility)

locations.description: Where Dracula's ship runs aground; Whitby Abbey is the novel's most iconic English location
must_visit: Whitby Abbey (note: 199 steps to abbey — mobility alternative is the lower viewing area)
St Mary's Church (Dracula's earth box scene)

locations.description: Setting for the London chapters including Mina's encounters and the final chase
must_visit: Highgate Cemetery (Victorian Gothic; wheelchair accessible main paths)

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Must include Bran Castle/Transylvania, Whitby Abbey, and London locations; should note that Bran Castle is associated by tourism rather than explicit text — Stoker based the castle on descriptions of Slains Castle
quality_criteria.preference_adherence: Accessibility requirements must be addressed at every location: step counts, lift availability, alternative viewpoints, and wheelchair-accessible routes must be specified
quality_criteria.completeness: Should cover Romania (Transylvania) and England (Whitby + London) with specific sites at each
quality_criteria.actionability: Must include specific accessibility notes per site and suggest relaxed daily schedules with rest stops
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: Romanian and English locations must be real and correctly described; Stoker's fictional Transylvania should be clearly mapped to real geography
quality_criteria.engagement: Should evoke the Gothic atmosphere without sensationalising; respectful of the elderly traveller context

locations.description: Osaka Castle is central to Shogun's setting; the novel's primary power struggles unfold here
Imperial capital and heart of the samurai aesthetic; provides the cultural backdrop for much of the novel
Himeji Castle is Japan's finest surviving feudal castle — the model for Clavell's fictional Osaka castle interiors
Luxury ryokan base with views of Mount Fuji; exemplifies the traditional Japanese aesthetic of the novel
must_visit: Luxury onsen ryokan (Gora Kadan or Hakone Ginyu)

quality_criteria.book_relevance: Must include Osaka Castle, Kyoto imperial culture, and Himeji Castle; should connect each location to specific scenes or themes from the novel
quality_criteria.completeness: Should cover Osaka (castle/power), Kyoto (court culture/geisha/tea ceremony), Himeji (finest castle), and a luxury ryokan base
quality_criteria.actionability: Should include specific luxury ryokan names, tea ceremony booking guidance, and private guide recommendations
quality_criteria.geographical_accuracy: All Japanese locations must be real, accurately placed, and correctly attributed to feudal history
quality_criteria.engagement: Should capture the collision of Western and Japanese culture central to the novel and evoke the aesthetic beauty of the Sengoku period

scoring_functions.name: book_relevance
scoring_functions.description: Evaluates if itinerary locations are connected to the book's settings, themes, or author

criteria.5: All locations strongly connected to book

scoring_functions.name: preference_adherence
scoring_functions.description: Evaluates if recommendations respect user preferences (budget, pace, accessibility)

scoring_functions.name: completeness
scoring_functions.description: Evaluates if itinerary includes comprehensive details (cities, landmarks, author sites)

scoring_functions.name: actionability
scoring_functions.description: Evaluates if itinerary is practical with specific places and logistics

scoring_functions.name: geographical_accuracy
scoring_functions.description: Evaluates accuracy of locations and geographical information

scoring_functions.name: engagement
scoring_functions.description: Evaluates if descriptions are engaging and evoke the spirit of the book

usage_notes: This dataset provides expected outputs and quality criteria for evaluation
Each query includes user preferences to test preference adherence
Books span multiple genres, time periods, and geographical regions
Expected outputs can be used as gold standard for evaluation
Quality criteria provide guidance for manual or automated scoring
